text:
Hydrogen ions (H⁺) form when a hydrogen atom loses its single electron, leaving a bare proton. This commonly happens when acids dissociate in water and donate protons, which attach to water molecules as H₃O⁺. The team note about phosphocreatine breakdown doesn't match this question. In muscle, the main acidifying source is lactic acid formation from anaerobic glycolysis and ATP hydrolysis, and phosphocreatine breakdown actually consumes H⁺ and buffers acidity.

CONFIDENCE: 72
